references.text: The woman's testimony that led many to believe: 'Come, see a man who told me everything I have done! Could he not be the Messiah?' (John 4:29). This is the testimony referred back to in verse 39.

After the Samaritans themselves had met Jesus, they said to the woman: 'We no longer believe just because of what you said; we have heard him ourselves' (John 4:42). The faith that began through the woman's testimony (v. 39) was confirmed through personal experience.

Jesus prays in his high-priestly prayer: 'I pray not only for them, but also for those who will believe in me through their message' (John 17:20). The woman's testimony that led others to faith is an early example of this principle.

Philip testified to Nathanael and said, 'Come and see!', and Nathanael came to faith (John 1:45-46). A similar pattern where personal testimony leads others to Jesus, just as the Samaritan woman led her fellow citizens to faith.
Many Samaritans came to faith through Philip's preaching (Acts 8:12). The Samaritans' receptiveness to the gospel has its background in the events of John 4.

'Many believed in his name when they saw the signs he performed' (John 2:23). A contrast: in Jerusalem many believed because of signs, while the Samaritans believed because of the woman's testimony – a word-based testimony.

Jesus said: 'Blessed are those who have not seen and yet have believed' (John 20:29). The Samaritans' initial faith (v. 39) came through the woman's oral testimony, pointing forward to the faith Jesus calls blessed.
'So then faith comes from hearing the message' (Romans 10:17). The Samaritans' faith came precisely through the woman's oral testimony – they heard her words and believed.
